correctness.rationale: Explicit marginal density is positive on (0,2), so the cdf is continuous and strictly increasing and the quantile transform is exactly the convex square map. The three atom expectile equations produce exact levels (3/7,3/5,3/4) and (5/7,1,6/5) with reversed secant slopes 5/3 > 4/3. The coupling score-strong-monotonicity lemma bounds perturbations by 15 eta and 60 eta. Expanding the determinant gives a quantitative error of at most 372 eta/7 + 7200 eta^2, strictly smaller than 3/350 for eta=10^-6. Thus the strictly positive determinant persists for the continuous model. The standalone verifier recomputes rational certificates. No part of the continuous proof relies on finite simulation.

value.rationale: Eberl–Klar Remark 6 motivates a genuinely stronger all-triplet expectile order and explicitly leaves unresolved whether conventional convex-transform ordering implies it. The finding gives a definitive negative answer inside the atomless strictly positive-density regime, not a finite discrete edge case, and separates robust scalar skewness consistency from failure of global transformed-expectile convexity. A quantified constructive smoothing argument supplies an explicit checkable counterexample useful for selecting admissible skewness-order axioms. No speculative extension or paper-sized claim is needed.
